title: Tutoring scope, authority and qualifications
audience: Tutors and education coaches (draft shell, no teaching content yet)
learningOutcomes: Describe what a tutor may and may not teach, and where the tutor's role stops and the school or the family's role starts.
Identify the kinds of qualification, registration or check that may apply to a tutoring role, and explain why the rule depends on the state or territory and on the work being done.
Record a written scope agreement with the client before the first session.

instruction.heading: What the engagement covers
instruction.body: A tutoring engagement is defined by its subject, the year level or skill, the goal the client has set, the place where sessions happen, and how often they run. Write each of these down before the first session. The tutor teaches the agreed subject to the agreed level and does not decide the school curriculum, change the learner's assessment tasks, or set goals the client has not agreed. If the client asks for something outside the agreement, such as help with a school assignment in a different subject, record the request and agree the change in writing before taking it on.

instruction.heading: Qualifications, registrations and checks
instruction.body: Some tutoring roles need a teaching qualification, a registration, a working-with-children check, or insurance. Whether any of these apply depends on the state or territory, the setting (a private home, a tutoring centre, or an online session), the age of the learners, and whether the tutor works through an employer or on their own. This lesson does not state those requirements. Treat each one as UNCONFIRMED until the rule for the exact role has been checked against the current official source and recorded with the date checked. Keep the evidence of each qualification and check on file.

instruction.heading: The scope agreement
instruction.body: Put the scope agreement in writing and have the client, or the parent or guardian of a learner under 18, sign or accept it through the business's recorded channel. It should state the subject and level, the goal, the session length and frequency, the location, who must be present for sessions with a minor, how progress is reported, and how either party can end the arrangement. Keep a copy with the client record. Review the agreement when the goal, the learner or the setting changes.

instruction.heading: When to decline or refer
instruction.body: Some requests fall outside a tutor's role. These include diagnosing a learning or medical condition, giving legal or financial advice, and taking charge of a learner who has no adult supervision. Where a request falls outside the role, decline it in writing, or refer the client to the professional who can help, such as the learner's teacher, a psychologist or a speech pathologist. Record the request, the decision and the reason for it.
